title: `ia validate` reports each `@execution-binding` as bound, unavailable or revoked against the catalog its host joined
summary: @inventarch/workspace-runtime adds the ./bind subpath (and ./internal/bind), exporting executionBindings(reader), executionBindingOf(record, resolve?) and bindExecution(binding, catalog) with the ExecutionBinding, BindingCatalog, BindingResult and BindingStatus types; a present BindingCatalog's operation rows are @inventarch/db/distribution's InstalledOperation, the catalog's one shape. executionBindings reads every admitted `@execution-binding` in the root view, sorted by identity, with its unconditional binding.kind, binding.implementation and binding.target resolved to an identity. bindExecution returns bound only when the catalog is present, lists the implementation as available, the binding is of kind operation and its target, when it names one, is the operation the implementation serves; unavailable when the binding names no implementation, its kind has no catalog section (only operation implementations are listed), the catalog is unavailable, does not list the implementation or lists it unavailable, or the implementation serves another operation; and revoked, an error, when the catalog revokes the implementation or failed verification. @inventarch/distribution adds joinedCatalog(root), which takes the catalog a host joined from the first join receipt whose host registration still names the joined release and whose payload verifies and carries the joined catalog digest, reports a payload that fails verification with changed or unlisted files, a link or exceeded limits as damaged, and is unavailable with the reasons when there is no receipt or none holds (an ia project-only workspace, a host registered by an earlier release, a drifted join, a payload without a catalog or not materialized); WorkspaceSession gains bindings(), which returns that catalog source (null when the workspace has no binding, and then nothing beyond the records is read) and one result per binding, and ia-distribution validate adds it to its result as bindings and exits 1 when a binding is revoked. @inventarch/cli's ia validate reports the same bindings: --json adds bindings, and the human report adds a Bindings section with the catalog source and one row per binding, a summary line counting unbound bindings as not a pass, and revoked bindings as errors that fail the run and the closing line; a workspace with no binding keeps its human report unchanged. ia doctor's implementations row names a revoked operation and warns. Computing and reporting bindings writes nothing, in the workspace or the IA home. Limits: nothing loads, imports, serves or executes an implementation (milestone 7 runs operations); only the catalog may revoke, since the `@execution-binding` schema has no revocation field; entry, hook and other non-operation bindings are always unavailable because the catalog lists no implementations of those kinds; a damaged joined payload revokes every operation binding, whatever implementation it names, while a missing payload file makes them unavailable; and ia validate's findings, counts, admission status and report outcome are unchanged, so a revoked binding fails the run without appearing among the findings.
